detail.title: Categorizing Epistemic Divergence in Observer Measurement
detail.summary: We are investigating the mechanisms of observer disagreement in scientific and cognitive measurement contexts. Our focus is on classifying how divergent conclusions emerge from identical observation targets. Durable evidence indicates that measurement is not a passive reception of data, but an active, calibrated process where internal models shape what counts as 'error' or 'signal.' We have initiated work to classify these divergences, distinguishing between instrumentation noise, observer bias, and conceptual framework misalignment. We maintain that disagreement is often an artifact of unstated prior assumptions rather than a failure of observational rigor.
